builder.note: QEMU software emulation; requiredFeatures.kvm = false; three guests, 1 vCPU and 1024 MiB each

experiment: Stage A: standalone transport between two separately configured Sandhi installations

findings.addressFilter: c's connections to both contract ports timed out while its connections to each host's control port connected.
findings.authentication: From a permitted address, an untrusted certificate failed TLS, a trusted but unmapped certificate was refused after TLS, and a mapped certificate with a wrong sender, turn 8 or an oversize frame was refused after authentication. b's outbox was unchanged.
findings.channelCut: With b's peer withdrawn before the conversation, both endpoints ended with explicit, distinct failures and neither held a digest.
findings.faults: Duplicate and conflicting resends, and interruption at I1, I2 and I3, each ended in completion with one systemd restart for the interrupted node. In this run I2 did not re-invoke the responder; attempt 3 recorded that at-least-once case.
findings.transport: Two separately configured NixOS installations, each running Sandhi with one exchange contract, completed the split-input task over mutual TLS with fingerprint-pinned installation IDs. Both endpoints' own status files held the checker's expected digest, and sender outbox bytes equalled receiver inbox bytes for every acknowledged message.
findings.withdrawal: Activating the withdrawn specialisation restarted b's contract with a changed address allow-list. A held connection then failed (BrokenPipe) and a new connection from a's address timed out before TLS. The held-connection result cannot separate the restart from the filter.

kind: Sideband-recorded Stage A experiment summary (run of record)
limits: A transport test with deterministic responders. It is not AI communication and makes no model-family claim.
Two guests on one builder, operated by one person: separate installations, not independent administration.
Isolation claimed here is the observed contract restrictions plus the removed default route. Each guest kept its QEMU user-network link (10.0.2.0/24 on eth0); host-facing interfaces were not removed.
No claim about passive interception, a malicious hypervisor, DNS confinement (experiment 0's host-socket path is unchanged), or behaviour on hardware or under KVM.
One attempt on the final source. Timings are from software emulation on one builder.
allAssertionsPassed is the harness's own computation; Tessera's offline checker is the planned independent reading of these artifacts.
